title: cog-compose-proposals input
description: The items and everything the judgment Cogs found, plus the next-up list that decides the order a human reviews the proposals in. Declared from the manifest as context.input_schema. This Cog reaches nothing: it is invoked with no grant.

items.description: The github-items artifact's items. A closed-context item is evidence for a duplicate claim and is never a proposal's target.

kind.description: Issue or pull request. Read to suppress a link between an issue and the pull request that closes it.

comments.description: Every comment body on the item, as cog-read-github read them. Read for ONE question: does the item already carry a comment marked with a link's change_id — `<!-- op-project-triage change:<id> … -->`, any run, either marker format? If it does, that link is already stated there and is skipped `already-satisfied` rather than proposed again (narrowing contract §16). Absent reads as no comments, which proposes exactly as before.

linked_item_ids.description: Every item id this item references, as cog-read-github normalized them: title, body, comments and reviews. A REFERENCE, not a closure — 'Related to #10, but does not fix it' puts #10 here. Suppression reads closing_item_ids instead (contract §11b).

closing_item_ids.description: The issues a PULL REQUEST declares it closes: GitHub's own closingIssuesReferences, read to the last page, and nothing else — no text anywhere makes a closure (contract §11c). An issue always states []. This — and only this — is what suppresses a link between an issue and its closing pull request.

overlap_findings.description: openteams/cog-overlap-duplicate-detector's payload, or null when that step was skipped.

dependency_findings.description: openteams/cog-dependency-detector's payload, or null when that step was skipped. Only `stated` dependencies are proposed; inferred ones are advisory and live in the next-up list.

overlap_provenance.description: openteams/cog-merge-findings' `provenance` from the merge-overlaps step, or absent/null when the findings did not come through a merge. Read for `cut_item_ids` alone: where a finding rests on an item cog-candidate-pairs shortened to fit a batch, the change's summary says so and its change id moves (narrowing contract §10). Declared loosely — an entry this Cog cannot fully read is still an entry.

finding_id.description: the merged overlap finding this describes

cut_item_ids.description: the items OF THAT FINDING that were shortened in a batch it was found in, sorted and de-duplicated; empty when nothing was cut

dependency_provenance.description: openteams/cog-merge-findings' `provenance` from the merge-dependencies step, or absent/null. Same element shape and the same use as `overlap_provenance`, for the dependency findings.

finding_id.description: the merged dependency finding this describes

cut_item_ids.description: the items OF THAT FINDING that were shortened in a batch it was found in, sorted and de-duplicated; empty when nothing was cut

classifications.description: The classify-items foreach step's payload: one openteams/cog-issue-classifier payload per item, null where that element failed.

next_up_list.description: openteams/cog-rank-next-up's payload. Used only to order the proposals, so the human reviews what is next first.

label_map.description: Which rubric value becomes which EXISTING label, per repository, and where this Op may propose at all: `inputs/label-map.draft.json`'s `repositories` object, passed in as an Op input so nothing here hard-codes it (narrowing contract §5). A label change is proposed only when the item's repository has `write: true` AND the rubric value maps to a non-null label, and the change's payload carries that exact label beside the kind and value it came from. Links follow the same `write` flag. Everything else is `skipped` with `repository-not-writable` or `report-only`. An absent map proposes NOTHING: the map is the only thing that says a repository is writable. This replaces the `type:`/`area:`/`priority:` namespaces, which this Cog no longer knows about.

write.description: Exactly `true` admits proposals in this repository — labels and link comments alike. Anything else, including an absent flag, is report only.

type.description: rubric type value -> an existing label in this repository, or null for report only.

notes.description: The team's own notes about this repository's label vocabulary. Read by people, never by this Cog.

closing_references.description: cog-read-github's meta.closing_references: `complete` or `incomplete` per repository. Where it is `incomplete`, closure is UNKNOWN rather than absent: nothing is suppressed there and the proposal's summary says so. Absent means complete.

marker_prefix.description: The prefix cog-write-github marks its comments with, so a link this Op has already commented is recognised here and never proposed again. Defaults to `op-project-triage`, and must be the same value the writer's bundle carries (narrowing contract §16).
